identity_rationale: Samuel P. Huntington, identified by The Soldier and the State: The Theory and Politics of Civil-Military Relations and Political Order in Changing Societies. Existing curated person ID reused; no new authority ID or namesake merger.

screening.role: Selection context only, not substantive proof or automatic identity resolution.

sources.note: New limited rereading of title/imprint and complete printed p. 1. Original copyright 1968, consulted seventh printing 1973. Distinction between forms and degree/capacity of government read directly; later pages not newly read completely. Earlier 1–7 and 12–13 review and its country-judgment/order-first qualifications preserved.

sources.title: Edward Said, The Clash of Ignorance, The Nation (4 October 2001; print issue 22 October 2001)
sources.note: Opening through discussion of personified Islam and West read: identifies Huntington’s summer 1993 Foreign Affairs article and criticizes suppression of internal diversity, exchanges and complexities. Rest of essay unread here. Online and print dates distinguished. Criticism attributed to Said, not treated as an impartial verdict or evidence that all readers agreed.

sources.title: Corydon Ireland, Samuel Huntington, 81, political scientist, scholar, Harvard Gazette (5 February 2009)
sources.note: Institutional obituary opening, selected work-date paragraphs and birth paragraph checked: born 18 April 1927, died 24 December 2008; Soldier and State 1957, Clash article 1993/book 1996. Its Political Order date 1969 conflicts with the read 1968 copyright and is not adopted. Remaining evaluative claims not imported.

substantive_relations.relationship: Distinguishes political capacity and institutionalization from regime form and economic modernization.
substantive_relations.note: Own Political Order opening p. 1 and preserved prior source review support the distinction. This does not endorse order-first political prescriptions or verify national comparisons and predictions.

substantive_relations.relationship: Criticizes the civilizational model for personifying Islam and the West and suppressing their internal diversity and exchanges.
substantive_relations.note: Said’s own 2001 essay opening read. Edge is Said’s specific criticism of Huntington, with explicit attribution; Huntington’s whole 1996 book and complete reception debate unread.

limits: Selected theoretical contributions and dated texts, with original, revised, translated and posthumous forms distinguished. Source notes state actual reading extent; no complete monograph or comprehensive reception survey is claimed. Existing collective relationships and source/roster qualifications remain.
